title: Students and youth strike across Croatia over living costs
seoTitle: Zagreb student strike over living costs

tea.why: High living costs, unaffordable housing, and lack of future prospects prompting youth to emigrate.
tea.want: Affordable housing, job transparency, and systemic changes to secure futures for youth in Croatia.
tea.changed: Nov 20: Education Minister Radovan Fuchs dismissed strikers as anarchists and announced unexcused absences.

summary: High school students and university students across Croatia launched a nationwide all-day boycott of classes as part of the International Youth Strike initiative, involving participants in more than 25 European countries. Organised independently by youth groups, the strike aimed to protest against soaring living costs, unaffordable housing, and limited opportunities that drive young people to leave the country. Representatives denied any political party affiliations or anarchist intentions. In response, Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs criticised the strikers as politically motivated anarchists and warned that students skipping classes would receive unexcused absences.
demands: Better conditions to keep youth in Croatia
response: Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs accused strikers of politicisation and being anarchists, warning that students who missed school would receive unexcused absences, according to N1.

updates.text: Students and high school pupils across Croatia were called to boycott classes for an all-day youth strike.
Education Minister Radovan Fuchs dismissed the protesters as politicised anarchists and threatened unexcused absences.
